title: quantization nan scratchpad - int8 fp8 bf16
content:
Context:
- Investigating intermittent NaNs seen in generation on int8-quantized llama-derived models. Repro rate ~1-2% on long prompts (~2048 tokens) in dedicated environment. No NaNs on bf16 baseline. FP8 experiments also show occasional NaN but different pattern.

Recent observations:
- NaNs typically surface after ~200-800 generated tokens, more common with longer KV cache usage and attention patterns that include many prefix tokens.
- Affected models: rwd-llama-3-7b-int8 (quantized by internal pipeline), rwd-llama-3-7b-fp8-experimental. BF16 build (non-quantized) is stable.
- Error symptom: downstream decoding loop sees logits containing NaN; generation loop throws and returns truncated sequence.

Commands / reproducer attempts (kept minimal):
1) Basic reproduction (dedicated node):
   $ python reproduce_gen.py --model rwd-llama-3-7b-int8 --prompt-file long_prompt.txt --max-tokens 1500 --batch 1
   Observed: 1/50 runs produced NaN at token 412.

2) Grep logs for NaN stack:
   $ rg "nan|NaN|inf" /var/log/redwood/runtime/*.log -n
   /var/log/redwood/runtime/2024-02-18.log:3452: WARN generation: logits contain NaN at step=412
   No stack trace. Logging point is in generation.py:emit_logits where we inspect logits before softmax.

3) Run with FP32 fallback for problematic attention kernel (manual env override):
   $ RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL=attention_fp32 python reproduce_gen.py --model rwd-llama-3-7b-int8 ...
   Result: run completed, no NaN. Reproduces only when using attention_fast_kernel (default for int8). Suggests kernel numerical instability.

4) Small-batch stress test with different sequence lengths:
   - seq=512: 0/200 runs NaN
   - seq=1024: 1/200 NaN
   - seq=2048: 4/200 NaN
   Pattern: higher seq => more likely.

5) Run with KV-cache clearing every N steps to test cache corruption hypothesis:
   - clear every 50 tokens: NaN rate drops significantly. (Implication: accumulation in KV cache or numeric drift).

6) Run with layer dropout/disable mixed-precision (disable quantization for first N layers):
   - force-first-4-layers-bf16: NaN rate reduced but not eliminated.

7) FP8 trials:
   - rwd-llama-3-7b-fp8-experimental shows NaNs earlier (~token 200) but more deterministic pattern across runs. Possibly different scaling calibration.

Error snippets (collected from logs):
- "WARN generation: logits contain NaN at step=412, layer=23, head=8"
- "RuntimeError: softmax received NaN"
- No OOMs, no GPU hardware errors reported by nvidia-smi or DCGM. No ECC memory errors.

Hypotheses / quick notes:
1) Attention kernel instability in quantized path (likely quantized matmul or rotary/ALiBi application). FP32 fallback eliminates NaN => kernel suspect.
2) KV cache accumulation + quantization scale drift: repeated requantize/rescale each step causes underflow/overflow leading to inf/NaN. Clearing cache reduces incidence supports this.
3) Per-head scaling in fp8 profile miscalibrated for long contexts (scales saturate).
4) Quantization code path may skip NaN checks for performance; small numerical issues propagate.
5) Memory reuse bug in kernel (stale buffers) causing invalid values when sequences longer or caching hits certain alignment boundaries.

Immediate next experiments (short term):
- Add aggressive NaN/inf checks right after each kernel (cheap path) to pin which kernel produces NaN. Instrument: LOG_ON_NAN=1 -> log tensor name, step, layer, head.
- Re-run reproducer with RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL=attention_fp32 and separately RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL=matmul_fp32 to isolate.
- Dump per-step KV-cache stats and tensor max/min/scale to analyze drift.
- Try a run with full fp16 instead of int8 to check whether quantization bits are the primary contributor.
- Run a kernel-level unit test with synthetic input stressing large prefix lengths and random attention masks.
- Reproduce on a different GPU type (A100 vs H100) to rule out device-specific behavior.

Longer-term / follow-ups:
- Audit quantization/rescaling code in serving-runtime: look for in-place ops that might alias memory between quantized and dequantized buffers.
- Evaluate switching to symmetric per-channel quantization for matmuls if asymmetric was used.
- Consider introducing periodic re-scaling of KV caches (re-normalize) as a mitigation if drift confirmed.

Notes to self (todo):
- [ ] Add NaN instrumentation to nightly smoke tests (dedicated cluster). Ticket: RDW-1287
- [ ] Create minimal reproducer that runs entirely on CPU for easier debugging (reduce GPU noise).
- [ ] Sync with Alex (kernel author) to review fast attention implementation (meeting Friday).
- [ ] Push patch to log full layer/head indices when NaN discovered (low overhead path).

Random logs / breadcrumbs saved here for context:
- github pr: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842 (attention kernel fast-path changes)
- linear: RDW-1287 (quantization nan investigation)
- slack thread: #eng-quantization thread id: C0234N8 (refer to 2024-02-18 messages)

If stuck, fallback plan:
- Roll out temporary policy: force fp32 attention kernel for int8 production models for contexts >1024 tokens until root cause resolved. Communicate impact on latency.

End of scratchpad.

-- maya
